cards.subject: A nerubian ziggurat
lines: Before it was a necropolis in the sky it was underground, in Northrend, and it belonged to the spiders. It was taken during the War of the Spider.
Kel'Thuzad was shown a vision of cultists tearing it out of the earth and lifting it. That is why there is an Arachnid Quarter — they were here first.

cards.subject: It is a wheel, not a corridor
lines: Every other vanilla raid is a line you walk down. This one opens four wings at once off a central hub.
The Frostwyrm Lair only opens when all four wing bosses are down, and it has no way out.
Hearthstone, or a summon. The building does not let you walk back.

cards.subject: Look up as you come in
lines: Every forty seconds three players are yanked across the room and cocooned against the far wall, suspended, while everyone else shoots them down.
The wall already has bodies on it before you pull.

cards.subject: He talks to you for weeks
lines: Kill a wing boss and a voice you cannot see answers. "Who dares violate the sanctity of my domain?"
Clear the wing and it changes: "You have seen nothing! The frozen heart of Naxxramas awaits you!"
He has been watching the whole clear.

cards.subject: A boss who is a floor pattern
lines: The room erupts in slow rolling waves of nature damage in a fixed repeating order, and you live by walking the safe strip as it moves.
Every couple of minutes he drives the raid onto the platform and runs it faster.
Whole raids died to a floor.

cards.subject: He is tanked by his own students
lines: He hits too hard for any player to hold, so priests mind-control his understudies and tank him with those, rotating as each priest is locked out.
Nothing else in vanilla is built this way.
Mid-fight he shouts "Sweep the leg! Do you have a problem with that?"

cards.subject: The room is cut in half
lines: Adds spawn on the living side. When they die their souls cross the gate and come back on the dead side, stronger.
Your raid is split by a fence and cannot help each other.
In 1.12 the undead half is immune to magic, so that side is melee or nothing.

cards.subject: It needed eight tanks
lines: Four bosses, four corners, two tanks each rotating out as their mark stacks — nothing, then two hundred and fifty, a thousand, three thousand, five thousand.
They stood about seven weeks before anybody killed them.
The wall was not skill. It was owning eight geared tanks.

cards.subject: The fourth horseman is Mograine
lines: The Wrath rebuild removes Highlord Alexandros Mograine and puts Baron Rivendare in the corner instead.
In here it is still him, and he carries the Corrupted Ashbringer.
This is the only place in the game that sword comes from.

cards.subject: The screams are not his
lines: A flesh construct wired into machinery. The raid splits by electrical charge every thirty seconds or dies.
The arena carries voices through the whole fight that do not belong to him. He is made of people.
When he dies he says "Thank... you..."

cards.subject: His name is an anagram of Healbot
lines: His curse puts a one-minute cooldown on every healing spell you cast. One heal per healer per minute, dispels included.
The whole raid lives on potions and bandages between the windows.
They named the healer-breaking boss after the healers.

cards.subject: Why everyone owned a second set of gear
lines: A blue dragon Arthas raised as a frost wyrm to guard the door to Kel'Thuzad. His aura is constant, unavoidable frost damage on all forty people at once.
That single aura is why frost resistance became an economy.
You farmed every other raid in the game for the materials to enter one room in this one.

cards.subject: Forty splinters make a frame
lines: Kel'Thuzad's underlings each had a chance at a splinter. Forty of them build the frame; the head comes off Kel'Thuzad and the base off C'Thun.
It is Medivh's staff. It comes in four colours, one per caster class, and it opens a portal to Karazhan.
The chain was gone before Naxxramas moved to Northrend.
